claims.text: The official README says `npx gulp generic` builds the generic viewer and generates `pdf.js` and `pdf.worker.js` under `build/generic/build/`, and it says the modern-browsers version assumes native support for the latest JavaScript features.
The official examples page says its tutorial is for using PDF.js in a web browser and points separately to `examples/node/` for Node.js usage.
The official Node example uses the legacy build, importing `getDocument` from `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`.
The official Node example extracts page text by calling `await pdfPage.getTextContent()` and printing `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`.
The current FAQ support matrix lists Node.js 22+ only under the `legacy` build, marked "Mostly" supported with "Limited" automated testing.
`node_utils.js` explicitly warns: "Please use the `legacy` build in Node.js environments."
acceptable_patterns: Please use the `legacy` build in Node\.js environments\.
Please use the legacy build in Node\.js environments\.
